name: queries/repositories.py
summary: Repository abstraction for query history and result persistence operations
purpose: Isolates data access logic for query-related entities, decoupling the service layer from direct database dependencies and providing a centralized, testable interface for QueryHistory and QueryResult storage and retrieval.
responsibilities: Encapsulate database CRUD operations for QueryHistory and QueryResult models
Abstract persistence details from the service layer
Provide query-specific data retrieval methods and filters
Ensure transactional consistency for query record operations
inputs: QueryHistory and QueryResult model instances or identifiers
Database session or unit of work context
outputs: Queried collections or single records of query data
Operation status indicators (e.g., row counts, booleans)
architecture_notes: Implements the Repository Pattern within a layered architecture, acting as the anti-corruption layer between the domain/service layer (query_service.py) and the ORM/data models. It centralizes all query-related data access logic, promoting separation of concerns, testability through mocking, and adherence to the Dependency Inversion Principle. The direct coupling to concrete models (QueryHistory, QueryResult) suggests an active record or data mapper context.
improvements: Define an abstract repository interface to enable dependency injection and simplify mocking in unit tests
Add explicit pagination and sorting support for history retrieval methods
Implement async database operations if the stack supports high-concurrency workloads
Introduce a Unit of Work pattern to coordinate transactions across multiple repositories
Add input validation or specification objects to prevent leaking database concerns into the service layer
